name: Copper Kettle Coffee Roasters
tagline: Small-batch specialty coffee, roasted every Tuesday in Austin
home: Copper Kettle is a small coffee roaster in East Austin. We buy green coffee from farms in Colombia, Ethiopia and Guatemala and roast it in small batches every week.
Order whole beans or ground coffee for your brewer, or join the subscription and get a fresh bag every two or four weeks.
about: We started in 2020 with a five-kilo roaster in a garage. Every bag names the farm, the altitude and the process.
Our roasts are light to medium: we want you to taste where the coffee comes from, not the roast.

posts.title: How to grind coffee for a French press
posts.description: The right grind for a French press without sludge or bitterness.
posts.body:
A French press needs a coarse grind, about like sea salt. Grind finer and the coffee slips through the metal filter, leaving the cup muddy and bitter.

## Ratio

Use 60 grams of coffee per liter of water.

## Time

Four minutes. Break the crust at one minute, skim the foam, and press slowly.

## Water

Just off the boil, around 200°F.

posts.title: Washed vs natural coffee: what's the difference?
posts.description: How processing after the harvest changes what's in your cup.
posts.body:
After harvest, coffee cherries are processed to get to the bean, and the process changes the flavor a lot.

## Washed

The fruit is removed and the beans are fermented and washed. The cup is clean, with bright acidity.

## Natural

The whole cherry dries in the sun for weeks. The bean takes on the fruit's sugars: sweeter, with berry notes and more body.
